# Test fixtures

Every fixture here is **invented**. None is a capture or a scrubbed copy of a
real record, document, study or provider response.

- `stream/synthetic.ndjson` is a `records-stream/v1` stream as a provider CLI
  writes it: 14 FHIR R4 resources for a synthetic patient, Robin Testperson,
  born 2020-02-02, at "Example Health" (`https://fhir.example.org/r4`). It
  carries two DocumentReference and Binary pairs, one of them an EOB that an
  ExplanationOfBenefit points at through `supportingInfo`, and its trailer.
  The Binary PDFs are generated by `medrec::pdfgen`.
- `stream/providers.ndjson` is the same kind of stream: visits, prescriptions
  (one in the STU3 shape), fills (one whose pharmacist has no display), a
  vaccine, procedures and a claim whose providers are named by reference, by a
  contained resource, by a role, by an absolute address on the source's own
  server and on another, by an inline identifier and by a reference to
  nothing. Its NPIs pass the check digit and start with 0, so they belong to
  nobody; one (`0000000007`) fails the check.
- `stream/shared-key.ndjson` is one of several streams with one CLI,
  organization and FHIR base. `testdata::shared_key_streams` fills in its
  `{{…}}`: each of two people as each of two patients, with the same records.
- `stream/fakeprov-info.json` is the `info --json` of `fakeprov`, the fake
  `health-records/v1` provider that `medrec::testdata::write_provider` writes.
  It lists the `login-profiles` capability. `fakeprov-info-unprofiled.json` is
  the same from before login profiles, `fakeprov-info-no-login.json` one
  that needs no login, `fakeprov-info-files.json` one that also reads
  downloaded files (`records-files`), and `fakeprov-info-files-only.json` one
  that reads files and signs in nowhere. `fakeprov-profiles.json` is its
  `profiles list --json` (`profile-list/v1`: `adult1`, `adult2`).
- `stream/summary.xml` is a synthetic clinical summary, shaped like one a
  portal renders on each export: `{{RENDERING}}` (its timestamp and document
  id) changes the bytes and not the text, and `{{FINDING}}` changes the
  text. `testdata::stream_with_summary` serves it as `doc-0001`'s Binary.
- `fhir/medication-dispense.json` is a pharmacy fill (MedicationDispense),
  coded by NDC and RxNorm, and `fhir/pharmacy-eob.json` the pharmacy claim
  for it (an ExplanationOfBenefit with CARIN's days supply and refill
  `supportingInfo`). Their NDC, `00000-0001-01`, is a dummy under the
  unassigned labeler `00000`. `fhir/medication-dispense-contained.json` is
  the same fill with its prescription contained, naming an `Example
  Prescriber`.
- `fhir/readings.json` is invented Observations at no one's, one for each shape
  of a result's value and of its parts, each with the value, unit, text, count
  of parts, codes of the parts with no value and categories expected of it.
- `fhir/left-out-line-eob.json` is a claim (an ExplanationOfBenefit at
  "Sample Rehab Center") of four lines, whose totals leave one out. Its two
  processing notes, one a line points at and one no line does, and its NUBC
  revenue code `0420` are invented.
- `fhir/stu3.json` holds invented FHIR STU3 resources in the shapes a
  behavioral-health EHR's patient API publishes: statuses as plain codes,
  `assertedDate`, `Immunization.notGiven` and `date`, `requester.agent`, one
  `DiagnosticReport.category`, and empty strings for absent values. Codes
  are `0000`, names are `Example …`.
- `nppes/npidata.csv` has the header row of CMS's public NPPES file and
  invented providers below it: their NPIs start with 0, their phones with 555,
  and one name holds a quote and one a line break. `nppes/page.html` is a
  listing page in CMS's shape, with links that must not be taken.
  `nppes/kept-v1.jsonl` is a kept directory as 0.9.6 writes one
  (`medrec-nppes/v1`), of two invented providers.
- `labels/` is an invented person's folder for the provider labels: claims, a
  portal visit and papers of invented practices, a mark, and `directory.jsonl`,
  the directory rows kept for it, with NPIs that start with 0. `providers.json`
  is the view they give.
- `standing/` is an invented person's conditions, allergies and medicines, one
  for each rule of "Standing" in `docs/data-contract.md`, at four invented
  places. `make.py` writes `household.json` and `index.json`, medrec gives
  `standing.json` from them, and `lists.json` is the lists a reader makes of
  it, each with the day, the records it may not show, and why.
- `errors/` is an invented person's records and papers entered in error, one
  of each kind the contract's "Entered in error" names, beside ones that stand
  and ones their sources differ on, with what the household decided of them
  (`marks.json`, `overrides.json`). `make.py` writes the files; their sources
  are those of `standing/household.json`.
- `given/` is an invented person's claim, stated by one source and given by
  another at a place of a private area, as the contract's "What a source gave"
  keeps it, beside one that is not private. `make.py` writes `index.json`; its
  sources are those of `standing/household.json`.
- `questionnaires/` is an invented person's results, one for each kind of
  questionnaire the contract's "Private" lists and one that is none, with a
  report and its paper, a paper named as one, a visit and claims of some of
  those days, and two pharmacy claims. `make.py` writes `index.json`; its
  sources are those of `standing/household.json`.
- `parts/` is an invented person's claims, procedures, bills and papers, one for
  each way the contract's "Private" reads a service and each kind of private
  part. `make.py` writes `index.json` and `text.json`; `parts.json` is what
  `private.json` says of the parts, an event's under a claim in it. Its sources
  are those of `standing/household.json`.
- `words/` is an invented person's records, one for each rule of the contract's
  "Private" by a record's own words and codes. `make.py` writes `index.json`. Its
  sources are those of `standing/household.json`.
- `bills/` holds invented text in the shapes `pdftotext -layout` gives a
  provider's patient statement and a payment receipt:
  `statement-columns.txt` puts the statement's fields in a header row over a
  row of values, `statement-inline.txt` gives each on its own line with a
  masked account number, and `receipt.txt` is a payment receipt. The two
  statements are one statement, read two ways.

- `bills/events.json` and `bills/papers.json` are an invented person's events
  and papers for the bill rules: a statement with copies and receipts, a bill
  and a later one from its biller, one no claim covers, a desk payment, and
  claims nothing has billed.
- `events/` holds invented people's indexes and texts for the event rules:
  `parent` and `child` (claims, portal records and papers, with each of the
  contract's kinds and rules), with `make.py`, `portal` (portal records with
  no claim) and `athena` (visits whose place a source does not name).
- `private/adult.index.json` and `adult.text.json` are an invented adult's
  records, written by `private/make.py`: one item private by each of the rules
  `code` (ICD-10 `F17.210`), `medicine`, `test` and `provider`, beside a
  condition, a medicine, a visit, a result and a visit summary no rule lists.
- `private/papers.json` is a list of invented bills, receipts and other papers
  with the text each gives: some private by their words, some by the paper
  they copy, follow or pay, and some no rule lists.

The scans, DICOM studies and the fake provider script are generated at test
time by `medrec::testdata` (and by `cargo run --example synth -- <DIR>` for
dogfooding).

The rules:
- People are `Testperson`, with birth dates 1990-01-01 and 2020-02-02.
- Organizations are `Example …`, at `example.org` and `example.com` hosts.
- Identifiers are obvious dummies (`pat-0001`, `MEMBER-0000000001`).
- DICOM UIDs sit under `2.25.0`.

Clinical codes (LOINC, ICD-10, RxNorm, CVX, CPT) are real public codes,
because they carry no personal data. `tests/fixture_shapes.rs` and
`tests/no_personal_data.rs` enforce these rules.

Never add a real record, study, header or screenshot here, scrubbed or not.
